Russian visas 
I spoke to an agency who helps with Russian visas. They said the best visa for us 
to get would be a business visa which is good for one year. They can apply for 
the invitation for us which takes 2 weeks to get. Once we have the invitation, we 
have to give our passports to the Russian consulate for 3 days to process the 
visa. All we have to give them for the invite is a copy of our passports, the 
company name, address, phone number and your position in the company. If we gave 
them that info today, we would have the invite by Dec 31st, but the Russian 
Consulate is closed from Jan 1-10, thus we could have the visas by Jan.13 at the 
earliest. The cost is $800 
Otherwise, if you want to stick with a tourist visa they are only good for one 
month and can be processed in a day.

I am sorry that this seems complicated. In New York apartment rentals usually 
require quite a bit of paperwork, even if the rent is prepaid. Usually a 
bank reference, employment, income verification and credit check are 
standard. The reason is the law in new york prevents the landlord 
from evicting the tenant. For example if the tenant chooses to stay on 
premises for months after the lease, the landlord can not enter the 
premises or force the tenant out, he has to wait for the courts to make 
a decision. 
I hope you understand that the questions Paolo is asking are not personal but 
standard new york procedure. I spoke with him and he said he is

I am sorry that this seems complicated. In New York apartment rentals 
usually require quite a bit of paperwork, even if the rent 
is prepaid. Usually a bank reference, employment, income

LANDMARK LAND COMPANY, INC. 
MEMORANDUM 
TO: 
Landmark Board of Directors, et. al. 
FROM: 
Jerry Barton 
DATE: 
December 17, 2010 
SUBJECT: 
Landmark - Update 
All, 
The most important thing first. We have sent all the information requested to the Durst 
Organization and it is being analyzed by Douglas' personal accountant. There have been 
almost no questions and the only request was for filll details on the appraisals of Barbados 
and South Padre Island. This request was because Douglas had hired an appraisal firm to 
review them. This is one area in which I have no concern. Although we have no cash, we 
have substantial value. Recently we received a note apologizing for the slowness of the 
review and asking us to be patient. You will recall Douglas committed that we would 
"know if we have a deal by Christmas." Obviously we expect news soon and i will let you 
know. 
Landmark produces cash flow in one of two ways; through sales or fees. Sales in 
Barbados will not help our cash immediately, because we must repay the bank loan before 
dividends. Sales in South Padre have been disappointing to me this quarter. Quality 
traffic is up, but to-date, sales are not. New fees, which have been non-existent the last 3 
years, will come when an investor decides to make a real estate investment in our area. In 
this regard, the wall of worry that built in the summer and fall has recently been 
disintegrated by the barrage of positive earnings reports. This opened up for the investors 
the slope of hope and we have received more interest in the last month or two than we 
have had all year. This demonstrates that investors are looking for opportunities to invest 
and we have what we believe is serious interest in Barbados, but as yet, nothing under 
contract. 
On a personal note, yesterday I drove through the snow to Johns Hopkins to have 3 more 
biopsies on my poor little foot; all in the same area, with the goal to define exactly what 
skin will be taken when I have the next and last operation. It is my hope that this will be 
done after Christmas, but before New Year's and I am told that the rehabilitation time that 
would limit travel, would be less. As the schedule becomes more certain, I will let you 
know.
